label: <DEL> step of short (L=3-4) sequences, esp. starting with 3
explanation: Fires only on the delimiter step (100% of mass at phase 1 / recall_idx 0), almost entirely in short sequences (L=3: 58% of mass, L=4: 37%). It never fires in the original or copy phases. Within those delimiters it is very selective (rate about 1.4% for L=3) and depends on token content: first token 3 (= token about to be output) gives 15x lift and 60% of mass, with c and 2 next. The last original token (prev_tok g, s, r, p, f, b) also raises the rate and magnitude. The strongest activations are 3 ... g <DEL> with L=3. Digit, w, h, x or t last tokens tend not to fire. The predicate (delimiter, L<=4, first token 3) has dev F1 0.38 and mass recall 0.56. Adding a prev_tok set raises precision to 0.64 but lowers recall, so the unit looks like a sparse conjunction of length, first token and last token, not one clean concept.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: 3, c, 2, b, q, l; least: u, n, -, s) and the previous input (most: g, s, r, f, y, b; least: o, x, v, c); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=3, L=3, t=3.
